qs.q: Allergic reactions differ from typical toxic responses because
o: They result from immune system stimulation releasing natural chemicals
They result from the chemical directly acting on cells
They only occur at high doses
qs.e: Allergic reactions are immune-mediated responses where the chemical stimulates the body to release natural mediators (histamine, leukotrienes, etc.) that cause the observed effects. Unlike toxic responses, allergic reactions don't always comply with dose-response assumptions and can occur at very low doses in sensitized individuals.
